[01:02] Keira: totally, we recommend using ephemeral service tokens for CI or vault-based secrets. pattern: CI fetches ephemeral token via machine-auth flow, token scoped to the sandbox project and short ttl. then rotate on every pipeline run. we have a snippet for github actions.
[01:18] Rajiv: are those ephemeral tokens compatible with our SSO? we use Okta and have strict lock down.
[01:23] Jon: yes you can wire the customer SSO to Redwood console for user auth on the control plane; for machine auth we support OIDC and ephemeral tokens. if you want full SAML/Okta service user mapping we can do that in Private deployments or via SSO integration for enterprise accounts.
[01:36] Sara: can you clarify encryption at rest? our security policy requires CMEK and HSM for key management.
[01:41] Ava: short answer: hosted supports provider-managed keys; for CMEK/HSM you should look at Private or Dedicated where we do KMS integrations and can use your HSM. ill mark this for the security deep dive.
